item.title: Ninety days, not three months: the EU rabies antibody deadline is counted to the date the animal health certificate is ISSUED (in force 22 April 2026)
item.description: Point 1(a) of Annex XXI to Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/692, as replaced in full by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/135 and applicable from 22 April 2026, requires the rabies antibody titration test to be carried out on a sample taken not less than 90 days before the DATE OF ISSUE of the animal health certificate. Article 14(c) of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/131 does not state the deadline itself: it cross-refers to that annex. Under the previous framework the same rule was written three different ways: Annex IV point 2(a)(i) of Regulation (EU) 576/2013 counted three months to the non-commercial movement; box II.3.1 of the certificate model counted to the date of issue of the certificate; footnote 8 of that same model counted to the date of import. Three calendar months are 89, 90, 91 or 92 days depending on the starting month, so the change is not cosmetic. Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/1052 of 12 May 2026 amended Annex XXI again (point 2(c)(i), Echinococcus) with effect from 12 August 2026 and is not yet reflected in the consolidated text on EUR-Lex. Verified 28 August 2026 against EUR-Lex and the official pages of fourteen EU Member State authorities and thirteen Latin American authorities.

item.title: EU pet import framework updated: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/131 supersedes 576/2013 (in force 22 April 2026)
item.description: As of 22 April 2026, non-commercial pet entry into the EU is governed by Regulation (EU) 2016/429 (Animal Health Law) and Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/131, with Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705 (animal health certificate and declaration models) and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/636 (territory and non-EU country lists). These supersede Regulation (EU) 576/2013 and Implementing Regulation (EU) 577/2013. Substantive requirements are unchanged: ISO microchip, rabies vaccination, RNATT/FAVN ≥ 0.5 IU/mL, 3-month wait. Transitional rule: 577/2013 certificates remain valid if issued before 1 October 2026. Zoovet Travel country guides, glossary and tools already reflect the 2026 framework.
